title: Memphis and its Necropolis
summary: Memphis, near Mit Rahina south of Cairo, was the capital of Egypt in the Old Kingdom, and its necropolis stretches along the desert edge as a chain of pyramid fields from Giza to Dahshur. UNESCO inscribed the property in 1979 for its pyramids, mastabas, rock tombs and temples.

uncertainty.note: Start is the beginning of the Old Kingdom, 2625 B.C. in the Penn source, when Memphis was the capital. The city and its cemeteries may be older and the Penn page gives no founding date. End is the present: the site survives.

as_recorded.value: capital city of Egypt during the Old Kingdom (2625-2130 B.C.)

reviewer_note: Least sure of the start: the Penn page dates the Old Kingdom capital only, and tradition places Memphis earlier. The pin sits on the open-air museum at Mit Rahina, 1 km from the UNESCO point; the necropolis itself spans some 30 km, hence 2 km uncertainty.
